newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's SEB says controls Brazil's ARNO.
newsitem.headline: France's SEB says controls Brazil's ARNO.

text.p: French domestic appliance maker SEB said it had bought for $153 milllion 93.3 percent of the voting shares in Brazil's ARNO and "has thereby taken control of the company."
SEB on April 4 announced that its public offer for 45 percent of the preference shares of ARNO had failed because almost none of the shares had been tendered.
SEB said in a statement it had bought the voting shares from a group of investors and was willing to buy the remaining voting shares at the same conditions.
SEB said that ARNO had 210,364 voting shares of which SEB now held 93.3 percent. ARNO also has 420,729 preference shares, without voting rights, of which SEB has 15 percent.
"SEB has therefore a total of 259,437 shares in ARNO which is 41.1 percent of the capital," it said.
ARNO had a 1996 turnover of 1.5 billion francs and a net profit of 165 million francs, employing 3,500 people at five sites in Sao Paulo.
